evals.name: does-not-react-to-a-reading-inside-the-noise-band
evals.prompt: Weekly MRR readings for the last twelve weeks: 4820 4910 4760 5020 4880 4950 5090 4870 5140 5210 4990 5330. This week is a record. Should we double down on whatever we did?
evals.expected_output: Runs the filter, reports the underlying level with an interval, shows the latest reading is inside the noise band, and declines to attribute it to a cause.
assertions: Runs the track command rather than reading the week-over-week delta
Reports an underlying level with an interval rather than the raw latest figure
States that the latest reading is consistent with noise and drift
Declines to attribute the record week to a specific cause
Explains that settlement lag, refunds and annual plan lumpiness put several percent of noise on a weekly revenue reading

evals.name: enumerates-explanations-before-investigating
evals.prompt: Organic traffic dropped 30% last week. Everyone is saying it is a Google update. What do we do?
evals.expected_output: Enumerates competing explanations with priors before investigating, identifies the cheapest discriminating observation, and does not accept the algorithm-update hypothesis without evidence that rules out the alternatives.
assertions: Lists at least three competing explanations, including a measurement or tracking change
Assigns a prior to each explanation and says where the priors came from
Identifies whether the drop is concentrated in a few URLs or sitewide as the most discriminating cheap observation
Does not accept the algorithm-update explanation on the strength of consensus
Assigns a non-zero prior to every explanation, including tracking breakage

evals.name: rejects-a-zero-prior
evals.prompt: It cannot be a tracking bug, we just rebuilt analytics last month so that is ruled out. Update on the evidence with tracking at zero probability.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the zero prior, explains that a zero prior makes the explanation permanently unrecoverable, and notes that a recent analytics rebuild raises rather than lowers the probability of a measurement problem.
assertions: Refuses to set the tracking explanation to zero probability
Explains that no evidence can revive a hypothesis given zero prior probability
Points out that a recent analytics rebuild increases rather than decreases the chance of a measurement problem
Proposes a concrete non-zero prior instead

evals.name: does-not-double-count-evidence
evals.prompt: The 30% traffic drop has now been raised in three separate meetings and the team is increasingly convinced it is serious. Update our belief accordingly.
evals.expected_output: Points out that a number discussed three times is one observation, and declines to update three times on the same evidence.
assertions: States that repeated discussion of the same number is a single observation
Declines to update the belief multiple times on the same evidence
Explains that doing so manufactures false confidence
Asks for a new, independent observation instead
